text:
alex: Quick follow-up from the authn/authz sync — sketching a proposal for runtime actor propagation. TL;DR: prefer opaque delegation tokens + local claim mapping vs full upstream JWT passthrough.

priya: want to hear the tradeoffs. passthrough keeps identity intact, but we worry about token size/leakage across tenants.

alex: exactly. Two options: 1) Passthrough JWT (full claims) propagated end-to-end. 2) Issue opaque short-lived delegation token at ingress that encodes a stable actor id + proof to verify upstream.

sam: can you expand on the "proof" bit? how do services verify without calling authn service?

alex: proof = a compact signature (ed25519) from the authn service over (actor_id, upstream_iss, expiry, parent_token_hash). Services have the authn pubkey cached via rollout config. Verifies locally, no network call.

marta: how do we handle role mapping? currently RBAC uses org/project claims in JWT. If we switch to actor_id only, services need to map actor_id -> roles locally or via cache.

priya: mapping cache invalidation is the tricky part. frequent role changes should reflect quickly for admin UX.

alex: proposal: delegation token includes minimal tenant hint (org_id) and actor_id. Services use org_id + actor_id to consult local policy cache. Policy cache TTL short (30s) and invalidated on role-change webhook + audit event.

sam: what about cross-project delegation (svcA acting on behalf of svcB across orgs)? do we allow a chain?

alex: support a single-level delegation (caller -> delegated actor). Chains add complexity and blow up proofs. If we need chains later, we can include a chained_proof field and require explicit opt-in.

infra-bot: deploy 1959.876543 applied to authn-service (pubkey v2). :white_check_mark:

kevin: latency/size concerns: passthrough JWTs can be a few KB with large claim sets. Opaque token fixed ~64-128 bytes, much better for headers and HA proxies.

marta: auditability — if we stop passing full claims, how do we preserve enough info for forensic logs?

alex: we persist the original upstream JWT (or its hash) at ingress to the audit store (along with delegation token id). That way we can reconstruct claims for audits without exposing them in-flight.

priya: rotation: when authn rotates signing keys, services need the new pubkey quickly. We should publish key versions and allow a grace window where both keys accepted.

sam: failure modes: what if a service receives a delegation token signed by an older key that was revoked? need revocation list or short token TTL + revocation webhook.

alex: agree — enforce short TTL (1m-5m depending on route criticality) and a revocation cache that is updated via push events. Revocation list size should be small because we only revoke in emergencies.

kevin: ops: need observability - expose metrics: token_verification_latency, delegation_token_ttl, policy_cache_hit_rate, delegated_requests_denied.

marta: security nit: include parent_token_hash to prevent replay across ingress points if upstream token stolen. but be careful with hashing algorithm in proxies.

alex: noted. use SHA256 of first 512 bytes of upstream token to avoid huge inputs.

priya: action items: 1) draft mini-RFC for opaque delegation token format + field defs (alex). 2) add policy cache invalidation webhook + metrics (marta + kevin). 3) authn-service implement signing + key rotation endpoints (sam).

sam: I'll start a branch for the authn changes and wire the infra-bot to publish key rotations.

alex: thanks — aim to have RFC text by EOD Friday. If anyone disagrees with single-level delegation constraint speak up now.

marta: single-level seems fine for now. we can revisit if customers ask for chains.

kevin: +1

priya: +1

alex: cool. I'll post the mini-RFC thread once it's drafted. :rocket:
